mutations.because: the row's rule is that a file is under 100 if ANY of the four metrics is, and branches is the one that earns its own entry: it is the only metric that can be under 100 while every LINE of the file was executed, so a file whose one unreachable `||` operand was never taken reports 100/100 lines and is not covered. Dropped from the list, `underHundred` finds nothing in a summary whose only short metric is branches, the coverage row exits 0, and the run reports the whole second-host check as settled on a branch with dead code in it — the exact verdict this tool exists to produce, and the only one an operator reads. The test the row names drives it: a summary whose sole shortfall is `branches: 99.5` must be LISTED and must exit 1, and with the metric gone the list is empty. Every other assertion in the file survives the mutation, which is why the anchor is the whole METRICS list and not a bare "branches": the 'Unknown' pct case reads lines, and the two-metric case reads lines and functions, so both still pass and cannot see this
command: a file at 99.5% branches is LISTED and exits 1, though every line ran

mutations.because: the empty-run check, and the only place a run of this tool can settle on code it never measured. A `--cover` glob that matches nothing — a typo, a path that moved, a glob a shell expanded away — makes vitest write a summary carrying the `total` aggregate and NO per-file entry. Every other question asked of that document answers it correctly and says nothing wrong: `shortFiles` finds no short file and returns an empty list, which is indistinguishable from a perfect run, so the coverage row would read as 100% and the whole second-host check would settle on a branch whose coverage was never taken. Answering `true` unconditionally is the fail-open this row exists to close: the item-1 test drives a summary with no per-file entry and requires the row to be red and to name the globs (`no file matched --cover …`), and with the check gone the row is green and the run's exit code is 0. The `total`-only document is why the predicate is `some(file !== 'total')` rather than a key count, and why the sibling test in coverage.test.ts asserts `shortFiles` on the same document returns an empty list — that second assertion is what makes the pair readable: the list is empty AND the run is still red
command: a --cover glob that matched nothing is red, naming the globs
